en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Nadrah, from Qays, who said: I said to 'Ammar: "What do you think of this deed of yours that you did regarding the affair of 'Ali? Is it an opinion you formed, or something that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, entrusted to you?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, did not entrust to us anything that he did not entrust to all people generally; but Hudhayfah informed me from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him; he said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: 'Among my companions there are twelve hypocrites; among them are eight who will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle: eight of them will be taken care of by the dubaylah, and four...'"—I did not remember what Shu'bah said about them.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's—they said: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: Ibn Abi Mulaykah reported to me that Humayd ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn 'Awf reported to him that Marwan said: "Go, O Rafi'—to his doorkeeper—to Ibn 'Abbas and say: 'If every man among us who rejoices in what he has acquired and loves to be praised for what he has not done is to be punished, then we will all certainly be punished.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: "What do you have to do with this verse? This verse was only revealed concerning the People of the Book." Then Ibn 'Abbas recited: {"And when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture: 'You shall surely make it clear to the people and not conceal it'"}; and Ibn 'Abbas recited: {"Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have perpetrated and love to be praised for what they have not done..."}. And Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, asked them about something, but they concealed it from him and told him something else; and they went out making him think that they had answered him about what he asked them, seeking praise from him for that, and rejoicing in what they had done by concealing from him what he had asked them about.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and Muhammad ibn Sahl at-Tamimi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far reported to us: Zayd ibn Aslam reported to me, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that men among the hypocrites during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, when the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, went out for a military expedition, would stay behind and rejoice in remaining behind the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. When the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, returned, they would present excuses to him, swear oaths, and love to be praised for what they had not done. So there was revealed: {"Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have perpetrated and love to be praised for what they have not done—do not think them safe from the punishment"}.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us; (and a different chain) Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to me: Ghundar narrated to us, both from Shu'bah with this chain of narration, similar to it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Adi—namely Ibn Thabit—who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Yazid narrate from Zayd ibn Thabit that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, went out to Uhud, and some of the people who were with him returned. The companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, became divided into two factions regarding them: some of them said, "We should kill them," and some of them said, "No." So there was revealed: {"What is the matter with you that you are two groups concerning the hypocrites?"}.

Abu Bakr ibn Khallad al-Bahili narrated to me: Yahya—meaning Ibn Sa'id—narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: Sulayman narrated to me, from 'Umarah ibn 'Umayr, from Wahb ibn Rabi'ah, from 'Abdullah; (and a different chain) he said: Yahya narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: Mansur narrated to me, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from 'Abdullah, similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar al-Makki narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: Three persons gathered near the House: two from Quraysh and one from Thaqif, or two from Thaqif and one from Quraysh, having little understanding in their hearts but much fat on their bellies. One of them said: "Do you think Allah hears what we say?" Another said: "He hears if we speak aloud, but does not hear if we speak quietly." The other said: "If He hears when we speak aloud, then He hears when we speak quietly." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {"And you were not covering yourselves lest your hearing, your eyes, and your skins should testify against you..."} the verse.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Yahya—namely al-Qattan—narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah with this chain of narration, similar to it, and he added: He said: "So he abandoned praying over them."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: When 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul died, his son 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and asked him to give him his shirt to shroud his father in, so he gave it to him. Then he asked him to offer the funeral prayer over him, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stood up to pray over him. 'Umar stood up and took hold of the garment of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, are you going to pray over him when Allah has forbidden you to pray over him?" The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Allah only gave me the choice, saying: {'Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times...'}, and I shall increase beyond seventy." 'Umar said: "He is a hypocrite!" Yet the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, prayed over him. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {"And never pray over any of them who died, ever, nor stand at his grave"}.

Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi narrated to me: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj reported to us: 'Amr ibn Dinar reported to me, saying: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came to 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy after he had been placed into his grave... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Sufyan.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ahmad ibn 'Abdah ad-Dabbi narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Abi Shaybah's; Ibn 'Abdah said: reported to us, while the other two said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr, that he heard Jabir say: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came to the grave of 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, had him taken out of his grave, placed him upon his knees, breathed some of his saliva onto him, and clothed him in his shirt; and Allah knows best.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us: Abu Ishaq narrated to us that he heard Zayd ibn Arqam say: We went out with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on a journey in which people suffered hardship. 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy said to his companions: "Do not spend upon those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse from around him"—Zuhayr said: and that is the recitation of those who read hawlihi with genitive. And he said: "If we return to Madinah, the more honorable will surely expel the humbler therefrom." He said: I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and informed him of that, so he sent for 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy and questioned him. He swore with great effort that he had not done it, and said: "Zayd has lied to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him." He said: Distress entered my heart from what they said until Allah revealed the confirmation of my truthfulness: {"When the hypocrites come to you..."}. He said: Then the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called them so that he might seek forgiveness for them, but they turned their heads away. And regarding His words: {"as if they were propped up pieces of wood"}, he said: they were men of the handsomest appearance.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: 'Affan narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Thabit reported to us, from Anas, that a man was being accused with the mother of the child of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to 'Ali: "Go and strike his neck." 'Ali went to him and found him in a well cooling himself off. 'Ali said to him: "Come out." He gave him his hand, and 'Ali pulled him out, and behold, he was emasculated, having no male organ. So 'Ali refrained from harming him, then came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is emasculated, having no male organ."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' both narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: When there was mentioned concerning my affair what was mentioned, while I was unaware of it, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stood to deliver a sermon. He recited the Tashahhud, praised Allah, and glorified Him as He deserves, then said: "To proceed: advise me concerning people who have accused my family, for by Allah, I have never known any evil from my family. And they have accused them regarding a person concerning whom, by Allah, I have never known any evil, and he never entered my house except when I was present, nor was I ever absent on a journey except that he was absent with me." And he related the hadith with its story, and in it: And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, entered my house and asked my slave-girl, so she said: "By Allah, I have never known any fault in her, except that she would sleep until the sheep entered and ate her dough—or she said her yeast"—Hisham was uncertain. Some of his companions rebuked her and said: "Speak the truth to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him," until they pressed her directly about it. She said: "Subhanallah! By Allah, I know nothing of her except what the goldsmith knows of pure unrefined red gold." The matter reached that man about whom it was said, and he said: "Subhanallah! By Allah, I have never uncovered the veil of any female ever." 'A'ishah said: And he was later killed as a martyr in the cause of Allah. And in it also was the addition: And those who spoke of it were Mistah, Hamnah, and Hassan; as for the hypocrite 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, he was the one who broadcast it and gathered it, and he was the one who took upon himself the greater share of it, as well as Hamnah.

Abu ar-Rabi' al-'Ataki narrated to me: Fulayh ibn Sulayman narrated to us; (and a different chain) al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd both narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, both from az-Zuhri, similar to the hadith of Yunus and Ma'mar with their chains of narration. In the hadith of Fulayh: "zealotry drove him rashly" as Ma'mar said; while in the hadith of Salih: "zealotry overcame him" as Yunus said. And in the hadith of Salih he added: 'Urwah said: 'A'ishah disliked that Hassan should be reviled in her presence, and she would say: "Indeed, he said: 'For indeed my father, his father, and my honor are a shield against you for the honor of Muhammad.'" And 'Urwah also added: 'A'ishah said: "By Allah, the man about whom was said what was said used to say: 'Subhanallah! By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I have never uncovered the veil of any female ever.'" She said: "Then after that he was killed as a martyr in the cause of Allah." And in the hadith of Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim: "traveling in the heat of midday", while 'Abd ar-Razzaq said: "muwghireen." 'Abd ibn Humayd said: I said to 'Abd ar-Razzaq: "What does he mean by muwghireen?" He said: "al-Waghrah is extreme heat."
